locked_decisions.decision: Group detail page: webapp pages (chains.py). Comment editing: webapp API (v1/shootouts.py) + pages (shootouts.py) + frontend template. Shootout ownership: webapp API (v1/shootouts.py or pages/shootouts.py). is_system_track cleanup: webapp pages/context.py + frontend Astro templates.
locked_decisions.rationale: Epic specifies this explicitly and matches codebase structure — group/chain pages in chains.py, shootout/comment endpoints in shootouts.py.

locked_decisions.description: Comment edit endpoint URL — epic says PATCH /api/v1/comments/<id> but existing comment routes are nested under /api/shootouts/{shootout_id}/comments/{comment_id}
locked_decisions.decision: Add PATCH at /api/shootouts/{shootout_id}/comments/{comment_id} following existing route pattern, not /api/v1/comments/<id>.
locked_decisions.rationale: All existing comment endpoints (POST create, GET list, DELETE) are nested under /api/shootouts/{shootout_id}/comments. A standalone /api/v1/comments/<id> would break the established routing convention and require a new router. The epic's URL was likely shorthand.

locked_decisions.description: Comment edit response schema needs updated_at field
locked_decisions.decision: Add updated_at to CommentResponse schema. The ORM model already has updated_at via TimestampMixin, and the domain entity has it. Currently CommentResponse omits it.
locked_decisions.rationale: CommentResponse (shootout_comment.py:28-39) currently lacks updated_at. The ORM model has it via TimestampMixin, the domain entity declares it. Needed for the edit use case to show 'edited' state.

locked_decisions.description: Comment edit request schema field naming — epic says {"body": str} but existing create uses {"content": str}
locked_decisions.decision: Use {"content": str} in the PATCH schema (a CommentUpdateRequest), matching the existing CommentCreateRequest field name and database column name.
locked_decisions.rationale: Domain entity and ORM model both use 'content'. CommentCreateRequest uses 'content'. The epic's 'body' was likely generic shorthand. Consistency wins.

locked_decisions.description: Where to add chain ownership validation for shootout creation
locked_decisions.decision: Add validation in shootout_create_submit (pages/shootouts.py) — the SSR form handler that actually creates shootouts with chains. Query SignalChain table to verify each chain_id is owned by current_user. Return 404 for any unowned chain.
locked_decisions.rationale: The JSON API create_shootout (v1/shootouts.py) doesn't accept chain_ids — only name, di_track_id, description. The SSR wizard form handler shootout_create_submit is where chain_ids are submitted and ShootoutChain entities are built. This is the only code path that associates chains with shootouts.

locked_decisions.description: Comment edit auth — existing delete returns 403 for non-author, but epic says edit should return 404
locked_decisions.decision: Comment edit endpoint returns 404 (not 403) when the comment exists but the user is not the author, following the epic's specification and the AGENTS.md rule ('Return 404 not 403').
locked_decisions.rationale: AGENTS.md security rules explicitly state: 'Resource access: always verify resource.user_id == current_user.id. Return 404 not 403.' The existing delete endpoint's 403 is actually a pre-existing violation of this rule that should be fixed as part of this work.

locked_decisions.description: Group detail page — the template exists but no SSR endpoint serves it
locked_decisions.decision: Add a GET /library/chains/group page handler in chains.py that queries the group by ID, verifies user ownership (404 if not owned), builds context, and renders fragments/library/group_detail.html.
locked_decisions.rationale: The Jinja2 template fragment exists (group_detail.html.ts). The group_item.html.ts template already links to /library/chains/group?id={{ group.id }}. The JSON API get_signal_chain_group already exists in signal_chain_groups.py. This just needs an SSR page endpoint in chains.py following the same pattern as library_chains_page.

locked_decisions.description: Group detail page context — the template expects group.name, group.description, group.base_chain, group.permutation_count, and a slots list
locked_decisions.decision: Create a group_to_detail_context function in pages/context.py that maps the ORM model to the template's expected context structure (group dict + slots list).
locked_decisions.rationale: Follows established pattern — every page has a context mapper in pages/context.py (e.g., chain_to_library_context, shootout_detail_context, gear_to_detail_context).

locked_decisions.description: Comment editing frontend — HTMX inline swap pattern for editing comments
locked_decisions.decision: Add an edit button (visible only when comment.is_own) to the comment template. Clicking it swaps the comment text with an inline form via HTMX. Submitting PATCHes to the API and swaps the updated comment back in.
locked_decisions.rationale: Epic specifies HTMX inline swap. The existing comments template already has is_own logic for the delete button. Following the established HTMX fragment pattern.

locked_decisions.decision: Remove from: (1) pages/context.py:108 hardcoded False, (2) frontend/astro/src/components/SignalChain/DITrackSelectModal.tsx:229 badge, (3) frontend/astro/src/lib/api.ts:489,505 type definitions, (4) frontend/astro/src/pages/fragments/library/track_item.html.ts:86,95 badge + delete suppression, (5) frontend/astro/src/pages/pages/di-tracks/detail.html.ts:66 badge.
locked_decisions.rationale: Grep found exactly these 5 files with is_system_track references. The field is hardcoded to False in context.py — no database column, no domain entity field. Pure dead code removal.

locked_decisions.decision: Add an update method to ShootoutCommentService following the same pattern as delete: look up comment, verify ownership (raise ValueError if not found), update content, return updated comment. Add corresponding update method to ShootoutCommentRepository.
locked_decisions.rationale: Service has create, list_by_shootout, delete. Repository has create, list_by_shootout, get_by_id, delete. Both need an update method for the edit feature. Following established patterns.

locked_decisions.description: No existing comment tests found in the test suite
locked_decisions.decision: Tests will be written as part of the epic's test generation phase. Key test cases: comment edit by author succeeds, comment edit by non-author returns 404, shootout creation with unowned chain returns 404, group detail page renders for owner.
locked_decisions.rationale: No comment tests exist currently. The epic workflow generates tests after plan approval.

locked_decisions.description: The existing delete_comment endpoint returns 403 when a non-author tries to delete, violating the project's '404 not 403' rule (AGENTS.md). The new edit endpoint will correctly return 404.
locked_decisions.decision: Change delete_comment to return 404 for non-author access, matching the ownership-check rule used for edit/create flows.
locked_decisions.rationale: Demoted by critique: This is already mechanically resolved by project policy and the report’s own rationale: ownership mismatches must return 404, and leaving delete at 403 creates inconsistent behavior and information leakage. It should not be user-choice.

locked_decisions.description: The group_detail.html.ts template references API endpoints that may not exist yet: DELETE /api/signal-chain-groups/{id} and POST /api/signal-chain-groups/{id}/generate. The JSON API has delete_signal_chain_group and generate_permutations functions.
locked_decisions.decision: Implement the SSR group detail handler and context mapper, render the existing template as-is, and verify existing delete/generate actions point to valid endpoints.
locked_decisions.rationale: Demoted by critique: This is answerable by code inspection and epic scope. The epic asks to wire the missing group detail page endpoint; it does not ask for a product decision on removing existing template actions. Keep existing template behavior and wire the route/context.

locked_decisions.description: The epic specifies PATCH /api/v1/comments/<id> as a flat route, but all existing comment routes are nested under /api/shootouts/{shootout_id}/comments/. The nested form requires the client to know the shootout_id.
locked_decisions.decision: Add comment edit as nested route: PATCH /api/shootouts/{shootout_id}/comments/{comment_id}, consistent with existing create/delete comment endpoints.
locked_decisions.rationale: Demoted by critique: This is a convention/mechanical decision, not a stakeholder preference. Existing comment routes are nested, the report already locked that decision, and the client already has shootout_id in context.
